unit_description: This unit explores the relationship between area and perimeter. Students find shapes with the same perimeter but different areas, the same area but different perimeters, missing sides, and solve real-world problems.
unit_goals: Find shapes with the same perimeter but different areas.
Find shapes with the same area but different perimeters.
Find area, perimeter, or a missing side.
Use area and perimeter to solve real-world problems.
Compare and contrast area and perimeter.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students compare area and perimeter, build shapes with equal area or perimeter, and solve real-world problems.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by drawing rectangles with a given perimeter and finding their areas.
lessons.concept: Different shapes can have the same perimeter but different areas. A long, skinny rectangle and a square can both have the same perimeter, but the square usually has more area.
lessons.practice: Find different rectangles with the same perimeter and compare their areas.
lessons.objective: Find shapes with the same perimeter but different areas.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by comparing perimeters and areas.

questions.prompt: Which has more area: a 1 by 11 rectangle or a 4 by 4 square?
Find the perimeter of a 4 by 4 square and a 1 by 7 rectangle.
A rectangle has perimeter 18. Which has more area: 1 by 8 or 4 by 5?

learn.title: Same Perimeter, Different Areas
teaching_points: Same perimeter does not mean same area.
Try different factor pairs for the same perimeter.
The closer to a square, the larger the area.

example.prompt: Perimeter = 16. Compare a 1 by 7 and 4 by 4 rectangle.
example.equation: 1×7=7 sq units, 4×4=16 sq units, both have perimeter 16

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Perimeter is 20. Which has more area: 1 by 9 or 5 by 5?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find two rectangles with the same perimeter and compare their areas.

flashcards.title: Same Perimeter, Different Area
flashcards.instructions: Review same perimeter and different area.

bigIdea.title: Same Perimeter, Different Areas
bigIdea.subtitle: Shape matters for area
bigIdea.intro: Two shapes can have the same distance around the outside but very different amounts of space inside. The more square-like the shape, the bigger the area for the same perimeter.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does a square give the most area for a given perimeter?

ruleCards.description: The sum of all sides is the same.
The area depends on how the sides are arranged.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by drawing rectangles with a given area and finding their perimeters.
lessons.concept: Different shapes can have the same area but different perimeters. A long, skinny rectangle has a larger perimeter than a square with the same area.
lessons.practice: Find different rectangles with the same area and compare their perimeters.
lessons.objective: Find shapes with the same area but different perimeters.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by comparing same-area rectangles.

questions.prompt: Which has the greater perimeter: a 1 by 12 rectangle or a 4 by 3 rectangle?
A rectangle has area 24. Find the perimeter of a 2 by 12 rectangle.
Area is 18. Which has the smaller perimeter: 2 by 9 or 3 by 6?

learn.title: Same Area, Different Perimeters
teaching_points: Same area does not mean same perimeter.
Squares have the smallest perimeter for a given area.

example.prompt: Area = 36. Compare a 1 by 36 and a 6 by 6 rectangle.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Area is 20. Which has a smaller perimeter: 1 by 20 or 4 by 5?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find two rectangles with the same area and compare their perimeters.

flashcards.title: Same Area, Different Perimeter
flashcards.instructions: Review same area and different perimeter.

bigIdea.title: Same Area, Different Perimeters
bigIdea.subtitle: A square saves perimeter
bigIdea.intro: When two shapes cover the same amount of space, the one that is more square-like has a smaller perimeter. Long, skinny shapes need more distance around.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why do long, skinny shapes have a larger perimeter for the same area?

ruleCards.description: The square has a much smaller perimeter.

lessons.lesson_title: Find Area, Perimeter, or a Missing Side
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by labeling what is given and what is missing for area and perimeter.
lessons.concept: Use the formulas for area and perimeter. If you know two of length, width, area, and perimeter, you can find the third. Area = length × width. Perimeter of rectangle = 2 × length + 2 × width.
lessons.practice: Solve for missing area, perimeter, or side lengths.
lessons.objective: Find area, perimeter, or a missing side.

questions.prompt: Length 8, width 3. Find the area and perimeter.
Area 24, width 4. What is the length?
Perimeter 30, length 9. What is the width?

learn.title: Find Area, Perimeter, or a Missing Side
teaching_points: Use inverse operations to find missing values.

example.prompt: A rectangle has length 7 and perimeter 22. Find the width and area.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle has width 5 and area 35. Find the length and perimeter.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find the missing area, perimeter, or side length for each rectangle.

bigIdea.title: Find Area, Perimeter, or a Missing Side
bigIdea.subtitle: Use the formulas and inverse operations
bigIdea.intro: Area and perimeter are connected by the length and width. If you know two of these values, you can use the formulas to find the others.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How are area and perimeter formulas related?

ruleCards.description: Multiply length by width to find area.
Add all sides, or use 2 lengths plus 2 widths.

lessons.lesson_title: Use Area and Perimeter to Solve Real-World Problems
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by deciding whether a problem asks for area or perimeter.
lessons.concept: Real-world problems use area when covering a space and perimeter when measuring a border or fence. Read carefully to choose the right measurement.
lessons.practice: Solve real-world problems that require area or perimeter.
lessons.objective: Use area and perimeter to solve real-world problems.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up with area or perimeter?

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to put a fence around a garden. Does she need area or perimeter?
questions.hint: A fence goes around the outside.

questions.prompt: A teacher wants to cover a wall with paper. Does she need area or perimeter?
A pool is 8 feet by 5 feet. How much tile is needed for the floor?

learn.title: Use Area and Perimeter to Solve Real-World Problems
teaching_points: Use the right units: linear for perimeter, square for area.

example.prompt: A garden is 9 feet by 4 feet. How much fencing is needed? How much soil is needed to cover it?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A poster is 6 feet by 4 feet. How much border tape is needed? How much paper covers it?
try_it.hint: Tape is perimeter, paper is area.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Solve each real-world problem. Decide if you need area or perimeter.

flashcards.title: Area or Perimeter?
flashcards.instructions: Review when to use area or perimeter.

bigIdea.title: Use Area and Perimeter to Solve Real-World Problems
bigIdea.subtitle: Choose the right measure
bigIdea.intro: Area and perimeter are used for different things. Area is for covering or filling a space. Perimeter is for going around the edge. Read each problem to decide which one to find.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do you know whether to find area or perimeter in a word problem?

ruleCards.description: Perimeter measures distance around the outside.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of same perimeter/different areas, same area/different perimeters, missing sides, and real-world area/perimeter problems.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: same perimeter different areas, same area different perimeters, finding missing values, and real-world problem solving with area and perimeter.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about area and perimeter relationships.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter 20. Which has more area: 1 by 9 or 4 by 6?
Area is 36. Which has a smaller perimeter: 3 by 12 or 6 by 6?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: same perimeter + same area + missing sides + real-world = area and perimeter relationships

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A garden is 7 feet by 5 feet. How much fencing is needed?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 24 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 24 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Area and Perimeter
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: same perimeter but different areas, same area but different perimeters, finding missing area/perimeter/side, and solving real-world area and perimeter problems.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about area and perimeter relationships?

ruleCards.description: The same perimeter can make different areas.
Area measures space inside; perimeter measures distance around.
